messages:
Maya: Quick heads-up — legal asked for a proactive note to the customer about how latency and uptime credits would work for their bespoke contract. They want a short plain-language paragraph + two sample months.
Ethan: Can grab the last 90d SLO numbers and anonymize incidents. ETA 2pm.
Sarah: I can scrub PII and format a sample calc. Will need the exact SLA matrix to map numbers.
Jon: For the wording, keep it non-legal. e.g., 'If monthly uptime falls below the committed threshold, a credit will be applied based on the shortfall and the committed monthly fee.' We should show one example with no credit and one that triggers credit.
Maya: Legal specifically asked: include whether we do latency-based credits (p95) or only uptime. Any precedent?
Ethan: Our standard SLA only covers uptime. We haven't had a commercial latency credit before. If legal wants it, we'll need SRE signoff on measurement method.
Jon: If adding latency credits, propose a simple trigger: p95 > 500ms for 3 consecutive days. Then show sample calc.
oncall-sre: Adding SRE context — if you propose a latency clause we need to agree measurement (region-level ingress p95, rolling 30d aggregation), define excluded maintenance windows, and decide whether cached responses are included. Also need a neutral fallback if telemetry gaps occur.
Maya: Good catch. Let's avoid double-dipping: propose latency-credit only applies when uptime remained above 99.5% that month. That prevents overlapping credits.
Sarah: Working draft plan: 1) include standard uptime tiers from our matrix, 2) a one-paragraph customer-facing explanation, 3) two table rows with sample months (numbers and final credit calc), 4) optional latency clause text with measurement notes. I'll draft and drop in Drive.
Ethan: Quick numbers from the dashboard (anonymized): 90d uptime 99.92%; p95 latency for gen endpoints ~420ms; two short incidents (total ~18 minutes) last month.
Maya: Perfect. Legal also asked for the exact formula we use. Jon, can you propose the exact arithmetic?
Jon: Suggest formula in the doc: credit = min( (committed_fee) * credit_rate, committed_fee ) where credit_rate derived from bracket shortfall. Example: if SLA is 99.9% and observed uptime is 99.75%, shortfall = 0.0015 (0.15%), credit_rate = shortfall / 0.001 (example mapping) -> 0.15 -> 15% credit. But we should map to our official matrix (tiered).
Sarah: I'll map the dashboard numbers to the official matrix. For example month A (99.92%) -> no credit. Month B (99.75%) -> triggers bracket 99.7-99.9 -> sample credit calculated and shown.
Ethan: Also flag: customer is on Dedicated (monthly commit). Credits should apply against the committed fee, not per-token usage. @acct-bill please confirm.
acct-bill: Confirmed — for Dedicated committed customers, SLA credits are applied as a credit against the monthly committed invoice.
Maya: Thanks. Ops follow-up: SRE sign-off needed if we add latency clause. oncall-sre — can you review proposed measurement language in the draft?
oncall-sre: Will review. Two requests: 1) define exact percentile window (p95 over 30d rolling, measured at ingress), 2) exclude scheduled maintenance windows with 48h notice. If that looks good we can sign off.
Sarah: Draft uploaded: https://drive.company/internal/CS/SLA-bespoke/draft-4958675309.pdf (internal). It includes the one-paragraph, sample calculations, and an optional latency clause with measurement notes.
Maya: I'll review and then loop in Legal. If Legal wants to include latency credits, we add SRE signoff as a condition.
Jon: Also propose adding a single-sentence 'how we measure' for the contract: 'Measured at regional ingress points, aggregated daily, excluding scheduled maintenance and force-maintenances acknowledged by both parties.'
Ethan: FYI I anonymized incident IDs and included links to the evidence bundle.
Maya: Next steps & owners: Sarah — finalize the 1-page customer brief + one-sentence contract blurb by EOD. Ethan — validate the numeric examples. oncall-sre — review latency clause by EOD. acct-bill — confirm application to committed fee (done). I'll loop in Legal after we have the draft. Follow-up standup tomorrow 10:00am. :thumbsup:
